title: The Mission of the Descending Lord
english: An apostleship occurring to men follows the glory of the one called God, being Almighty; for he was not sent as Almighty, but in the manner of 'emptying himself' and 'taking the form of a servant' by descent. What is being pre-announced to those still at their peak while being plundered by nations? 'He who touches, he says, of you, touches the apple of his eye' (Exodus 4:6), harming himself rather than striking the righteous or those he intends to harm, similarly to the one striking the apple of his own eye. This theory gathers from many places of Scripture: Cain, wishing to harm, exposed himself before he intended to murder (Genesis 4:8). The same happened to Saul pursuing David in order to kill (1 Samuel 24:1-22), and to Absalom attacking his father tyrannically (2 Samuel 15:1-14).

In the present prophetic [text] it signifies harming through touching, and especially through those whom God himself says to those attacking murderously against his own people: 'Touch not my anointed ones, and do evil to my prophets' (Psalm 105:15). To touch lightly lies in: 'It is good for a man not to touch a woman' (1 Corinthians 7:9), signifying approaching shamefully and licentiously. From this verb it is also shown that to touch well is to join through contact, as in that said by Jesus: 'Someone touched me' (Mark 5:27), when the woman with the issue of blood, desiring to be healed, touched by grasping the hem of Jesus' garment. Having fallen so many [interpretations] upon the present voice of 'touching,' the now present prophetic word signifies harming through maltreatment. But he who intends evil against those guarded by God touches the apple of the eye of the inner man. And it is manifest how he who touches the servants of God touches the apple of his own eye, because of the saying: 'I will lay my hand upon them' (Ezekiel 28:26), making manifest the disciplinary power, so that they become plunder to those they formerly plundered, leading them into captivity, so that they serve those against whom they formerly ruled tyrannically. Which event [leads to] 'you shall know that I am the Lord Almighty' (Ezekiel 20:23), having been sent by the Lord Almighty, is the completion of the things pre-announced. The God Word is being sent Almighty from the Almighty, coming to men by the good pleasure of the Father.

title: The People of God and the Inheritance of Judah
english: The Lord has come and has tabernacled in her midst, the temple having been raised again and God dwelling in it. 'Rejoice and be glad,' says the prophet, 'daughter of Zion.' In many places of the Scripture, the daughter of each city is called, meaning the citizens who fulfill her.

The delight and the gladness which the divine word commands to have is the same as the joy which happens to be the fruit of the Holy Spirit, arranged together with divine love and blessed peace, which the holy Apostle makes manifest writing thus: 'The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace' (Galatians 5:22). Having experienced this stability, those delivered from captivity say: 'When the Lord turned the captivity, we became as those who are returned; then our mouth was filled with joy, and our tongue with shouting' (Psalm 126:1). And in another Psalm it is brought in harmony: 'When the Lord turns the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice and Israel shall be glad' (Psalm 126:3).

For those who mourned, being torn away from their own fatherland by the law of captivity, follow a return to it, to delight and be glad because the Lord has tabernacled in its midst, the cause of the delighting and the gladness. And what is the cause of the gladness and delight—is it the enjoying of the currents of the river filled with waters, about which it is written: 'The river of God was filled with waters,' and also: 'The currents of the river make glad the city of God; God is in its midst, it shall not be moved' (Psalm 46:4-5), no longer departing or abandoning, but because of goodness remaining with it?

And what good and salutary will attach to the indwelling of the Lord in the midst of the beautiful city, or the 'fleeing of many nations' repenting 'unto the Lord in the day' when the sun of righteousness is grasped, of which the patriarch Abraham, having received light, seeing it, rejoiced, and with him the sons and children of him who are according to faith and his works having become, as saying thanks: 'This is the day which the Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it' (Psalm 118:24). And the 'many nations having fled unto the Lord' shall receive the people to enrich the one to whom they have fled, no longer atheistic and without hope.

remaining; concerning these things God says in the prophet: 'I will call him who is not my people my people, and he himself will say: Lord my God you are' (Hosea 2:23), so that they may be addressed as 'a holy nation, a holy priesthood, a race of God' (Exodus 19:6).

For he says to those fleeing to God in the same manner as mentioned by him to whom they have fled: 'You shall be to me an elect race, a holy nation, a royal priesthood, my people, through whom I shall display my virtues' (Exodus 19:6).

What then follows for those who have become the people of God, or the dwelling in the midst of the heavenly and blessed Zion? For then then it will be known, by divine and accurate vision, 'that the Lord Almighty sent' (Isaiah 60:22) the one redeeming her, saying concerning his own Father: 'The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he anointed me to preach to the poor, to proclaim release to the captives' (Luke 4:18).

For because of preaching to the poor, Jesus, who dwells in the midst of Zion, was anointed with the Holy Spirit and the power of God, proclaiming release to the captives held by unseen enemies, her children. For thus the All-King, the benefactor of her, will inherit Judah, those who confess. For the confession of Judah is interpreted. And so he will first inherit those called unto salvation; for from of old they were part of him and before that they suffered dispersion and captivity.

But where will he inherit Judah being part of him, except upon the holy land in which he will be long-enduringly well-suffering, he who honors his Father God and his Mother the Church being Jerusalem, whom he still loves, taking again and reigning in her midst, knowing that he has come to dwell in her midst, sent from the Lord Almighty, when bowing heaven he descended to us humans, saying: 'I have descended from heaven to do the will of him who sent me' (John 6:38), 'to seek and to save the lost' (Luke 19:10).

For thus they will no longer remain in perdition, for whom he has come, so that he might become the cause of eternal salvation for them. And the Jerusalem being fulfilled by us as the Church of the living God shall also have such a faith and works making beatitude, so that he who washed and brightened her with his own blood may still love her.

title: The Light Cloud of the Incarnation
english: Her. 1.168 Zach. 2:17: Let all flesh stand in awe before the face of the Lord, because he has been raised from his holy clouds. 1.169 The term 'flesh' being homonymous signifies many things, as it stands for the God-breathed writing itself. For when it is said in the Psalms, 'To give food to God to all flesh' (Ps 50:12), it stands for all mortal animals being sustained by food in living, as also in: 'All flesh is gathered according to its kind' (Gen 15:28). And when the Apostle writes: 'For who has ever hated his own flesh? But nourishes and warms it' (1 Cor 12:3), the body joined to the rational soul is signified, as it is possible to learn from the apostolic word itself having this: 'In this manner men ought to love their own wives as their own bodies. For who has ever hated his own flesh?' (Eph 5:28), and the following.

1.170 But there is also when only men are revealed by the designation of flesh, as in: 'Hearken to prayer, to you all flesh shall come' (Joel 2:28). And it comes to God in relation and disposition, not the irrational, but the humanity, being made worthy of the bountiful gift of the Holy Spirit by the one saying: 'I will pour out from my Spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy' (Joel 2:28). 1.171 This so-called flesh, being rational, is receptive of divine awe; for indeed, 'to stand in awe from the face' of the one appearing to it is commanded, concerning which the pure of heart, saying, send up a prayer: 'Appear your face and we shall be saved' (Ps 41:2). And he gives the reason hereafter for why all flesh ought to stand in awe before the face of the Lord God, bringing forth: 'Because he has been raised from his holy clouds' (Zach 2:17).

1.172 But holy clouds are not those that cause sensible rain, but those that bring the spiritual downpour, according to that said in Isaiah concerning Israel, by way of allegory called a vineyard, from the face of the Lord: 'I will command the clouds not to rain upon it' (Isa 5:2), because of the thorns and not having grapes as fruit. 1.173 For of the vineyard being allegorized, the clouds were also taken up in harmony, sometimes raining to water, sometimes being prevented from doing this. Concerning such rain-givers, again in that same prophet, it is commanded by God:

“Let the clouds rain down righteousness.” For since righteousness is a virtue of the rational soul, it is not the sensible clouds that pour rain, but the divine prophets, being called clouds by upward analogy.

Since therefore the Savior has come forth from these clouds to fulfill the law and the prophets, for this reason “let all flesh stand in awe from the presence of the Lord” (Ps 96:1) the God, which was predicted and shown when the prophecy having this character was fulfilled: “The God of gods shall be seen in Zion” (Ps 50:5), and he shone so that “we might behold his glory, as the only-begotten from the Father” (Jn 1:14).

Having come forth from the holy clouds, which were interpreted to be Moses the great hierophant and the prophets who possessed the Holy Spirit, he arrived upon a light cloud, having mounted upon the world which is among us, Egypt which is called by analogy. And the prophecy concerning these things begins from this place: “Behold, the Lord sits upon a light cloud, and he shall come into Egypt, and the works of her hands shall be shaken” (Isa 19:1).

Having been transferred from Egypt to the place concerning the earth, in harmony the light cloud shall be raised to the humanization of the Savior, the God the Word sitting upon that which had gone forth from Mary.

For what light cloud does not have the weight of sin, or the flesh of Jesus which did not consist of the union of man to woman being heaviest, but from the Holy Spirit having come upon the virgin not having experience of man, and upon whom the power of the Most High overshadowed, to make the born one holy without marriage. And even more the lightness and thinness of the lordly cloud is revealed from the fact that it was not made by sin nor did the soul of Jesus know it.

For nothing else drags and weighs down the soul of men like lawlessness, being compared to a talent of lead, because it searches and drags down those practicing it; but the soul of Jesus was not tried by this weight, “having loved righteousness and hated lawlessness” (Ps 119:160); nor did he have “neither deceit in his mouth” (Ps 33:13) which scatters the sins of all, the one having it.
